messages:
kai: Heads up: perf sig in cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel bump. Seeing ~6% drop on web-search cohort. Anyone else?
perf-bot: Profile summary: KV cache hit-rate decreased from 78% -> 72% on cohort 'web-search-v2'. p95 latency +18ms. Heatmap: https://internal.redwood/heatmaps/3845678901
marta: Is this cache keying issue or batching change? The kernel bump touched scheduling.
sam: I ran `kvcache:stats` on a node, found spike in unique prefix keys per hour. Looks like toolcall arg ordering changed for some clients. Example diffs: `{"tool":"search","args":["q","filters"]}` vs `{"tool":"search","args":["filters","q"]}`
rachel: We rolled tokenizer v3.1 yesterday to optimize kernels; could be subtle tokenization diffs leading to key churn.
kai: @rachel can you confirm tokenizer shard mapping? Also which flag toggled? Did we unpin vocab?
rachel: We only changed the merge table for emojis, but didn't repin. However some SDKs pulled a new tokenizer via CDN. I'll check rollout % now.
devon: I dumped top 1k keys, lots vary only by whitespace and system prompt order. Example: `prefix: syst=role:HUMAN prompt:'Hello'` vs `prompt:'Hello' syst=role:HUMAN`. We should canonicalize ordering before hashing.
marta: Agree. Quick wins: 1) stable sort of metadata fields before hashing 2) canonicalize whitespace 3) add tokenizer-version into key. Rollout plan?
kai: Plan: hotfix to normalize ordering + add tokenizer tag to key. Roll forward to 10% traffic as canary. If hit-rate recovers, 100%.
sam: Concern: adding tokenizer version to key will increase cardinality for mixed clients (temporary dip). Maybe use a fallback bucket: if token_version missing, treat as legacy. Also we can warmup/backfill for top 10k prefixes to avoid cold misses.
marta: We have a backfill tool. I'll run warmup for web-search cohort after canary. Need list of top prefixes; @perf-bot can you export?
perf-bot: Exported top_prefixes_web-search-v2.csv -> s3://redwood-logs/prefixes/3845678901/top_prefixes_web-search-v2.csv
devon: Also kernel selection may affect batching heuristics; observed longer batch queueing causing misses on low-latency paths. Suggest we keep latency-critical routes on old kernel during canary.
kai: Good call. Add route-level kernel pin in routing table for canary.
rachel: One more: tool/function call args ordering — some SDKs started sending map instead of array. We need to normalize the tool field serialization in cachekey layer (stable stringify + sorted keys).
sam: I'll PR normalization util: sort object keys, stable stringify. I'll run the fuzz harness and unit tests.
marta: :thumbsup: Timeline: today - PR + unit tests, canary tomorrow morning, warmup after canary, full roll Friday if green.
kai: Thanks. Add notes to runbook and update console dashboard with a temporary metric `cachekey-mismatch:count`.
perf-bot: Alert created: cachekey-mismatch:count -> dashboard /dash/cachekeys/3845678901
